message.content: {"0": {"original": "The proposed Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) was defeated in a pleny", "rephrased": "The European Parliament decisively rejected the secretive Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA), with 478 votes against the measure compared to only 39 in favor, while 165 members chose to abstain from the final decision on this controversial trade deal.", "summary": "The European Parliament decisively rejected the secretive Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA)."}, "1": {"original": "cautioned that Karel de Gucht deferred any decision on how the Commission will", "rephrased": "The UK's Open Rights Group cautioned that the European Commission, led by Trade Commissioner Karel de Gucht, has deferred any decision on the future of the Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) until a European Court of Justice ruling confirms the deal's compatibility with European law.", "summary": "The Open Rights Group warned that the European Commission delayed its decision on ACTA pending a legal ruling."}, "2": {"original": "ACTA provoked massive rallies and demonstrations across Europe, with a peti", "rephrased": "The Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) provoked massive public opposition across Europe, evidenced by widespread demonstrations and a petition that accrued two million signatures against the secretive legislation.", "summary": "The Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) provoked massive public opposition across Europe."}, "3": {"original": "ACTA failed because its vague terms threatened civil liberties, such as border", "rephrased": "The Guardian's technology editor Charles Arthur argued that the Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) failed because its vague terms threatened civil liberties, such as border searches for copyright content, while ignoring real risks like fake drugs.", "summary": "Charles Arthur argued that ACTA failed because its vague terms threatened civil liberties."}}
